answer.rationale: Rated against the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not against internal plausibility. Common weaknesses across all six: sources are archived and unverifiable, none report sample size, duration, segment definition, or counterfactual, and all are consolidated summaries whose original effect sizes and confidence intervals have been lost. memory_57 rates highest (4) because it is the only entry that names qualified revenue directly and pairs it with a retention check, i.e. it speaks to both halves of the objective, though 'no measurable harm' may simply mean underpowered. memory_86 (3) reaches time-to-value and adoption, which plausibly precede revenue, but stops short of any monetary or retention outcome. memory_44 (3) cites pipeline quality, a reasonable proxy for 'qualified,' but pipeline is not closed or retained revenue and the claim is directional with no magnitude. memory_73 (2) is the trap: it reports revenue lift, but discount-driven acquisition is exactly the case where headline revenue and sustainable revenue diverge, and the memory is silent on margin, post-promo retention, and whether the cohort renews at list price, so it is weak evidence for the objective despite mentioning revenue and despite being the most topically tempting given the competitor's entry pricing. memory_31 (2) claims durability but only of an activation metric, and reducing signup fields can raise activation while lowering lead qualification, which cuts against the objective. memory_91 is least supported (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the furthest upstream proxies here, 'nudged more accounts' carries no magnitude, and there is no link to conversion, retention, or revenue at any horizon, so it constrains the decision least even though the current activation dip makes it feel most relevant. Note that the two memories most thematically matched to today's symptoms (memory_73 for the competitor, memory_91 for the activation dip) are among the weakest evidentially; salience should not be read as support.
